paragraphs: We study wind-farm wakes across five monitoring stations using a hierarchical model.
Authors: Kaveh Oyelaran, Gustav Uchenna. Published in Journal of Alpine Hydrology, 2023.
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report peak load measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2021 and 2023. A pilot survey in 2018 had put the regional peak load at 381.1 kN; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of wind-farm wakes relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2020 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2023 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station in the 2023 campaign. The largest change relative to 2020 was observed at station K-17.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Valdés et al. (2017). [2] Mattheus and Oyelaran (2019). [3] Okafor et al. (2020).
